S-duality

Words: 18
String duality OurBigBook.com
An S-duality relates descriptions at different coupling strengths. In type IIB superstring theory, SL(2,Z) acts on the axion-dilaton and string charge doublets.

NS5-brane (TNS5​=(2π)5gs2​α′31​)

Words: 18
String theory OurBigBook.com
An NS5-brane has five spatial dimensions and is magnetically charged under the Neveu–Schwarz two-form. Its string-frame brane tension scales as gs−2​.

Fundamental string (TF1​=1/(2πα′))

Words: 25
String theory OurBigBook.com
A fundamental string is the perturbative string of a string-theory description. Its string tension is the displayed expression in the string metric. It couples to the Neveu–Schwarz two-form.

Hagedorn temperature (TH​=βH−1​)

Words: 273 Articles: 2
String theory OurBigBook.com
If a density of states has high-energy growth proportional to a power of energy times eβH​E, its canonical Boltzmann sum fails for β<βH​. The Hagedorn temperature is the corresponding threshold. The open bosonic string mass spectrum and large-level degeneracy of an open bosonic string give βH​=4πα′​ in units with Boltzmann's constant, the speed of light and Planck's constant set to one. Polynomial prefactors affect behavior at the threshold itself; the growth alone does not distinguish a limiting temperature from a phase transition.

Thermal winding instability of a closed bosonic string (mth2​=β2/(4π2α′2)−4/α′)

Words: 78
Hagedorn temperature OurBigBook.com
Euclidean finite temperature compactifies time to a circle of radius Rβ​=β/(2π). The string oscillator ground states with zero momentum number and winding w=±1 have the displayed mass from the bosonic string mass spectrum. They become massless at βH​=4πα′​ and tachyonic at higher temperature. This thermal winding mode diagnoses breakdown of the perturbative low-temperature string gas at the Hagedorn temperature. The endpoint and order of a transition require interactions and a suitable stable vacuum; the ordinary zero-winding bosonic tachyon is already unstable independently of this thermal threshold.

Finite canonical partition function at the bosonic Hagedorn threshold (Z1​(βH​)<∞butZ1​ is nonanalytic at βH​)

Words: 123
Hagedorn temperature OurBigBook.com
For a critical closed bosonic string in 25 noncompact spatial dimensions, the smoothed string oscillator rest-mass density behaves as ρ(M)∼CM−26eβH​M, with βH​=4πα′​. At large M, the centre-of-mass momentum integral of e−βM2+p2​ is asymptotic to (2πM/β)25/2e−βM, up to the convention for phase-space measure. Thus the high-mass tail of the one-string canonical partition function is proportional to ∫M0​∞​M−27/2e−(β−βH​)MdM. This converges at β=βH​ but fails for β<βH​. Expanding about the endpoint gives twelve finite derivatives and a nonanalytic term proportional to (β−βH​)25/2; the thirteenth derivative diverges. Consequently exponential state growth does not imply divergence of the partition function at the threshold itself. The discussion assumes the separate infrared instability of the bosonic tachyon has been regulated and does not claim a stable bosonic thermal vacuum.

Brane (p-brane)

Words: 722 Articles: 13
String theory OurBigBook.com
A brane is an extended object with p spatial dimensions. Its history is a (p+1)-dimensional worldvolume embedded in target spacetime. A point particle has p=0, a string has p=1, and a membrane has p=2. Geometric brane actions depend on the induced worldvolume metric; D-branes also carry open-string endpoint and gauge-field data.

Four-dimensional supermembrane

Words: 135 Articles: 1
Brane OurBigBook.com
The four-dimensional minimal supersymmetric membrane has embedding coordinates (Xm,θα) with four real odd components. Its area term uses the supertranslation-invariant superspace coframe, and a Wess-Zumino brane coupling integrates a superspace three-form potential with closed four-form curvature. Equal charge magnitude and tension permit kappa symmetry. After worldvolume reparametrization and kappa fixing, one transverse scalar and one three-dimensional Majorana fermion remain. This gives the long-wavelength description of the translation and fermion zero modes of a supersymmetric domain wall; it is distinct from restricting the eleven-dimensional M2-brane to a four-dimensional target.

Supermembrane closed four-form (G4​ ∝ iΠm∧Πn∧dθˉγmn​dθ)

Words: 59
Four-dimensional supermembrane OurBigBook.com
The four-dimensional membrane Fierz rearrangement identity (Cγmn​)(αβ​(Cγn)γδ)​=0 makes the displayed supertranslation-invariant four-form closed. It is locally the exterior derivative of a three-form potential, which can change by an exact form under target supersymmetry. Pulling the potential back to a closed worldvolume gives an invariant Wess-Zumino brane coupling. The charge magnitude and normalization of this form are fixed together by cancellation of the area variation under kappa symmetry.

Dirac membrane action (S=−T∫d3ξ−deth​)

Words: 55
Brane OurBigBook.com
A relativistic membrane sweeps out a three-dimensional worldvolume with induced worldvolume metric hij​=∂i​Xm∂j​Xnηmn​. Its leading geometric action is tension times its invariant volume. In static gauge in four-dimensional spacetime, one transverse field Y gives hij​=ηij​+∂i​Y∂j​Y, and the matrix determinant lemma gives S=−T∫1+∂i​Y∂iY​. Its rest-frame supersymmetry algebra has eight fermionic creation operators, producing 28=256 states. The massive little-group representations are 44+84 for the bosons and a 128-dimensional vector-spinor for the fermions.

The resulting 128 states form a gamma-traceless Spin(9) vector-spinor, of dimension 9⋅16−16.

String theory OurBigBook.com
A D-brane is a hypersurface on which open-string endpoints obey Neumann boundary conditions tangentially and Dirichlet boundary conditions transversely. Its massless open-string vector mode is a worldvolume gauge field.

D-brane OurBigBook.com
A type-IIB D-brane with five spatial dimensions. Its RR charge is magnetic with respect to the two-form potential C2​, or electric with respect to the dual six-form potential. It is distinct from the NS5-brane, whose charge is magnetic under the NS-NS two-form and whose string-frame tension has a different power of the coupling.

D-brane OurBigBook.com
A Euclidean type-IIB D-brane localized in all spacetime directions, coupling electrically to the RR scalar C0​. It is an instanton, not a Lorentzian particle with negative spatial dimension. The magnetic partner of that scalar charge is a D7-brane.

A space-filling type-IIB D-brane. The associated ten-form potential is nonpropagating; its charge is not an additional local massless polarization. A consistent compact configuration must cancel any net space-filling RR charge, for example through appropriate other charged objects or projections.

D-brane OurBigBook.com
A type-IIB D-brane with seven spatial dimensions. Its RR charge is magnetic with respect to C0​, or electric with respect to the dual eight-form potential. Its transverse geometry is codimension two, so the simple asymptotically flat rp−7 harmonic formula for lower-dimensional D-branes does not apply unchanged.

For the asymptotically flat extremal Dp solution with p<7, H=1+Q/r7−p is harmonic away from the source and eΦ=gs​H(3−p)/4. The electric potential can be chosen as C0⋯p​=gs−1​(H−1−1); magnetic descriptions use the dual flux, and a D3-brane has self-dual five-form flux. An equally oriented probe has DBI density −μp​gs−1​H−1 and Wess-Zumino density +μp​gs−1​(H−1−1), whose sum is position independent. This proves the corresponding parallel D-brane no-force identity in the classical background. The supergravity approximation requires controlled curvature and coupling; it does not resolve every brane core.

D-brane OurBigBook.com
Identical, parallel, equally oriented type-II D-branes preserve the same sixteen spacetime supercharges. Their annulus oscillator sum has the displayed numerator, which vanishes by the Jacobi abstruse identity. In the closed-string channel this is cancellation of attractive NS-NS exchange and repulsive RR exchange. The force vanishes in the flat supersymmetric configuration; anti-oriented branes, relative angles or supersymmetry-breaking backgrounds need not have this cancellation.

Dirac-Born-Infeld action (−Tp​∫e−Φ−det(P[G]+P[B]+2πα′F)​)

Words: 513 Articles: 8
D-brane OurBigBook.com
The Dirac-Born-Infeld action describes the leading derivative dynamics of one D-brane, including nonlinear dependence on slowly varying worldvolume field strengths. Its induced tensors are D-brane worldvolume pullbacks. The combination P[B]+2πα′F is invariant under the combined two-form and boundary gauge transformation. The dilaton factor reflects a disk's Euler characteristic. Expanding about flat space with small field strengths and embedding gradients gives the worldvolume gauge and scalar kinetic terms. A coincident stack has a non-Abelian low-energy Yang-Mills action; this does not imply that a naive traced determinant is exact at every order.

With Ei​=2πα′F0i​, this normalization separates the nonlinear constitutive relation from the D3-brane tension. It is the normalized canonical electric momentum. The Gauss law constraint in gauge theory requires its divergence to vanish away from string endpoints. On the electric BIon locus it equals the scaled electric field, but this equality is not true for arbitrary configurations.

A supersymmetric spike of a D-brane combines a worldvolume gauge field with a transverse scalar profile. Its geometry and charge represent strings ending on the brane. Words: 65
Born–Infeld soliton OurBigBook.com
The DBI action resums field strengths but truncates their derivative expansion. A slowly varying large-charge throat may therefore be controlled even when its field strengths are not small. Large derivatives, large embedding curvature, string loops and gravitational backreaction restrict this description, and its ideal singular core is not uniformly controlled. The electric throat window ∣N∣gs​≫1, gs2​∣N∣≪1 and magnetic window ∣N∣≫1, gs​∣N∣≪1 separate derivative and backreaction requirements.

Electric charge quantization gives c=πgs​∣N∣α′ and coefficient ∣N∣TF1​; magnetic charge gives c=π∣N∣α′ and coefficient ∣N∣TD1​.

It bounds energy by the electric scalar charge and is saturated at d=∇X. The opposite orientation uses the analogous identity with reversed signs. On saturation, the constitutive relation gives E=d and the Gauss law constraint in gauge theory reduces to the Laplace equation for X.

Words: 61
Dirac-Born-Infeld action OurBigBook.com
For Hermitian scalar matrices, their commutator is anti-Hermitian, so −Tr[ϕI,ϕJ]2=Tr[ϕI,ϕJ]†[ϕI,ϕJ]≥0. Dimensional reduction gives FIJ​=i[ϕI,ϕJ], fixing the minus sign before the literal commutator square inside the conventional overall-negative Yang-Mills action. Commuting scalar expectation values minimize this potential and describe ordinary separated branes. A plus sign instead requires interpreting the squared symbol as the positive Hermitian norm, not literal matrix multiplication.

Worldvolume fields from open-string massless states

Words: 57
D-brane OurBigBook.com
A massless open-string vector polarization tangential to a planar D-brane becomes a worldvolume gauge field. Transverse polarizations become scalar fields describing fluctuations of its position. This supports the interpretation of a Dirichlet plane as a dynamical extended object. The unprojected bosonic open-string tachyon additionally signals that its brane ground state is unstable; the massless field interpretation does not remove that instability.

Chan-Paton factor

Words: 51
D-brane OurBigBook.com
An endpoint label attached to an open string. With several coincident branes, two endpoint labels organize the massless open-string fields as matrices and give nonabelian gauge symmetry. Strings between different stacks carry representations associated with the two endpoint groups. These labels are physical internal degrees of freedom, not extra spacetime coordinates.

Open string stretched between D-branes

Words: 274 Articles: 4
D-brane OurBigBook.com
An open string stretched a distance L between parallel D-branes has squared mass M2=T2L2+(N−1)/α′. The stretching energy makes strings between separated branes massive.

Bosonic stretched-string tachyon threshold (d0​=2πα′​)

Words: 86
Open string stretched between D-branes OurBigBook.com
For two static parallel D-branes separated transversely by d, the open bosonic string mass spectrum becomes M2=d2/(4π2α′2)+(N−1)/α′. The classical stretching contribution is the square of the string tension times the separation, while the oscillator vacuum contributes the intercept term. Thus the ground state is a tachyon for d<2πα′​, massless at equality, and massive above it. Its real rest energy, when stable, is d2/(4π2α′2)−1/α′​; the vacuum correction belongs to energy squared and is not an additive fixed subtraction from the stretching energy. Angled branes change oscillator moding and require a different formula.

Words: 63
Open string stretched between D-branes OurBigBook.com
A commuting diagonal expectation value has one transverse eigenvalue vector for each brane. In the covariant derivative normalization Da​ϕ=∂a​ϕ+i[Aa​,ϕ], the off-diagonal gauge field has mass m2=∑I​(ϕ1I​−ϕ2I​)2. The corresponding stretched string has mass ∣X1​−X2​∣/(2πα′) in its massless oscillator sector. Equality fixes the displayed scalar-position normalization, up to a common coordinate origin. The trace describes center-of-mass motion and the eigenvalue difference describes separation.

Coincident-D-brane gauge enhancement

Words: 101 Articles: 1
Open string stretched between D-branes OurBigBook.com
When n parallel D-branes coincide, oriented strings joining distinct branes become massless alongside strings whose ends lie on one brane. Their Chan-Paton labels fill the adjoint representation of U(n), enhancing U(1)n to U(n).
Bosonic D3-brane low-energy field content (Aa​,ΦI (I=1,…,22))
Words: 66
Coincident-D-brane gauge enhancement OurBigBook.com
For coincident D3-branes in the critical 26-dimensional bosonic string theory, the massless open-string oscillator has a four-dimensional gauge vector and 22 transverse scalar fields. Chan-Paton factors put all these fields in the adjoint of U(k) for k coincident branes. Ignoring the tachyon, their leading interactions are the dimensional reduction of 26-dimensional Yang-Mills theory. This contains a Yang-Mills sector but is not pure four-dimensional Yang-Mills theory and is not the supersymmetric six-scalar D3-brane theory of the ten-dimensional superstring.

A conformal primary operator is annihilated at the origin by every special conformal generator. Acting with translation generators produces its conformal descendants.
